# Get penguins data set as object in environment to start
peng <- penguins

Question 1

Part A

Inspect data object using glimpse(). This function allows me to view the data and its qualities such as number of columns, number of rows and data types in each column. Additionally you are shown the head of each column (entries for each).

# Use glimpse
peng |> glimpse()
## Rows: 344
## Columns: 8
## $ species           <fct> Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adel…
## $ island            <fct> Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgerse…
## $ bill_length_mm    <dbl> 39.1, 39.5, 40.3, NA, 36.7, 39.3, 38.9, 39.2, 34.1, …
## $ bill_depth_mm     <dbl> 18.7, 17.4, 18.0, NA, 19.3, 20.6, 17.8, 19.6, 18.1, …
## $ flipper_length_mm <int> 181, 186, 195, NA, 193, 190, 181, 195, 193, 190, 186…
## $ body_mass_g       <int> 3750, 3800, 3250, NA, 3450, 3650, 3625, 4675, 3475, …
## $ sex               <fct> male, female, female, NA, female, male, female, male…
## $ year              <int> 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007…

Part B

There are \(8\) column variables. This is indicated by the column field in the glimpse() output.

Part C

Species is a qualitative variable. This is because it represents a quality or characteristic of what is being measured versus a numerical value or quantity. In other words, the species of the penguin is a grouping of the penguins based on a characteristic.

Part D

There are \(344\) penguins measured in the data set as shown by the number of rows in the glimpse() output.

Part E

Here I filter the penguin data set for the Adelie species and pipe this subset into ggplot. From there I set the aesthetics to have bill depth as \(x\) and bill length as \(y\). I make the data appear as points (accounting for NA values), add a title and my name and facet_wrap by island to get three separate plots for each island.

# Filter for Adelie species and make plot accounting for NA values and use facet_wrap to get plots side-by-side
peng |> 
    filter(species == "Adelie") |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = bill_depth_mm, y = bill_length_mm)) + 
    geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) + 
    labs(title = "Adelie Species Bill Length Versus Bill Depth",
         subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm") +
    facet_wrap(~island)

Question 2

First I use mutate to create new columns for bill length z-scores and z_class ID. This way I have the raw z-scores and then the groupings for each by outlier status. I use case_when to perform the logic on grouping assignment:

# Create new column for z-scores of bill length
peng <- peng |> 
    mutate(z_bill = as.numeric(abs(scale(bill_length_mm))), 
           z_class = case_when(z_bill > 3 ~ "Outlier", 
                               z_bill >= 2 & z_bill <= 3 ~ "Possible outlier", 
                               z_bill < 2 ~ "Main line"))

Next I filter the data set to get all data where z_class is not NA (removes NA entry from appearing on legend). This gets piped directly to ggplot where the aesthetics are \(x\) as bill depth and \(y\) as bill length. The data are represented as points and I add a title and my name to the plot:

# Create plot first by filtering out NA (prevents NA from being in legend) and using zclass to color-code
peng |> 
    filter(!is.na(z_class)) |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = bill_depth_mm, y = bill_length_mm)) +
      labs(title = "Outlier Detection of Bill Length Versus Bill Depth",
          subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm") +
      geom_point(aes(col = z_class))

Question 3

I create the plot by first filtering bill depth greater than 17. This gets piped to ggplot and the aesthetics are set to \(x\) as species and \(y\) as bill depth. I use geom_boxplot so the data is represented as boxplots (where fill color is by species) and use facet_wrap to get separate plots by island:

# Create plot
peng |> 
    filter(bill_depth_mm  > 17) |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = species, y = bill_depth_mm)) +
      labs(title = "Bill Depth by Species on Each Island - Boxplots",
          subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm") +
      geom_boxplot(aes(fill = species)) +
      facet_wrap(~island)

Question 4

To create the following table I use group_by to group the data by species and then summarise with the arguments for n as number of penguins in each species group, meanD as mean bill depth for each species and sdD as the standard deviation of bill depth for each species:

# Create summary showing mean and sd for bill depth grouped by species
peng |> 
      group_by(species) |> 
        summarise(n = n(), meanD = mean(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 
                  sdD = sd(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE))
## # A tibble: 3 × 4
##   species       n meanD   sdD
##   <fct>     <int> <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 Adelie      152  18.3 1.22 
## 2 Chinstrap    68  18.4 1.14 
## 3 Gentoo      124  15.0 0.981

Question 5

I used drop_na to remove NAs from the entire penguin data set. I then piped this to ggplot and set the aesthetics to have x as sex and y as bill depth. I used geom_violin with fill color by sex to get the data represented as violin plots. I then added a title and my name and used facet_wrap to get separate plots by species and island:

# Create plots using drop_na, geom_violin and facet_wrap
peng |> 
    drop_na()|> 
      ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = bill_depth_mm)) +
      geom_violin(aes(fill = sex)) +
      labs(title = "Bill Depth by Species on Each Island - Violin Plots",
          subtitle = "Jason M. Klemm") +
      facet_wrap(species ~ island)
